themes.dark: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) on :root:not([data-theme="light"]); each colorMeta entry carries its `dark` value

title.purpose: Commit subject in detail, session heading, dialog titles (16px/600). Empty-state headings 15px, toolbar repo name 14px bold.

body.purpose: Base size for rows, buttons, inputs, menus, toasts (13px/1.45).

label.purpose: Column headers, sidebar section headings, status chips (12px/600, sentence case, no tracking).

meta.purpose: Field labels (500), commit meta, hints, notices, session progress (12px).

badge.purpose: Ticket, merge and in-target badges (11px on an 18px line).

mono.purpose: Hashes, dates, counts, paths, branch route, conflicted files, diff. Cascadia Mono ships with Windows 11 and Windows Terminal and holds up better at 12px than Consolas, which is the fallback. Tabular figures.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, export menu and toast only; docked panes never cast shadows.

shadows.name: row-active-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard-active history row while the list is not focused.

shadows.name: row-active-focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard-active history row while the list has keyboard focus.

shadows.name: session-current-ring
shadows.purpose: Commit currently being applied in the session list, over blue-soft.

focus.input: outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: -1px; border-color: transparent

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: Loader icon while fetching or applying.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables toast-in and spin

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Workspace 200px | minmax(380px,1fr) | minmax(320px,30%); author column hidden; during a session the author column returns (112px) to carry the pick status and the date shows only the day.

narrative.overview:
Cherrypick Masive is the category standard on purpose: a three-pane git client (branches, history, detail) built for Windows developers who backport commit sets several times a week. The user chose the canon over invented directions, and the quality bar is GitHub Desktop and Fork. That means the system wins on craft, not novelty: honest hairlines, a disciplined 30px control height, tabular monospace columns that line up, and a single blue that means "selected" or "the next thing to do".

The history list is the work surface. Everything else serves reading it: the sidebar picks the branch, the filter bar narrows it, the right pane explains the focused commit and is replaced by the session panel while a cherry-pick runs. Density is high (13px body, 34px rows) and long-session legibility comes from neutral ground, low-chroma panes and strong ink rather than from whitespace.

State is the one place colour is allowed to speak, and it never speaks alone. The build refuses dashboard cards, metric tiles and decoration; a light and a dark scheme carry the same roles through the same custom properties.
keyCharacteristics: Three fixed panes on a neutral ground, separated by 1px hairlines, no floating cards.
One blue for selection, focus and the primary action; nothing else is blue except tickets and diff hunk headers.
Status colour is always icon + word + tint, never a bare dot or swatch.
Cascadia Mono for every hash, date, count, path and diff line, with tabular figures.
Light and dark schemes mirror each other role for role (`prefers-color-scheme`, overridable with `data-theme="light"`).

rules.name: The Word-With-Every-Colour Rule
rules.body: A status colour always arrives with an icon and a word: Applied (circle-check), Already there (circle-minus), Skipped (skip-forward), Conflict (octagon-alert), Pending (dashed circle, dashed outline, no fill), Applying (spinning loader). Colour without the word is a defect.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue means selection, focus or the primary action. Do not use it for decoration, headings or secondary buttons.

rules.name: The Data-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: If a value is compared down a column or copied into a terminal (hash, date, count, path, branch), it is set in the mono face with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Panes-Don't-Float Rule
rules.body: Nothing docked in the shell casts a shadow. Only overlays do.

dos: Do keep every control at 30px and every history row at 34px.
Do pair every status tint with its lucide icon and its word: Applied, Already there, Skipped, Conflict, Pending, Applying.
Do set hashes, dates, counts, paths and diffs in Cascadia Mono with tabular figures, falling back to Consolas.
Do separate panes with 1px hairlines (#d0d7de light, #30363d dark) and tonal steps, not shadows.
Do define every new colour as a custom property with both a light and a dark value.
Do keep a visible 2px blue focus indicator on every focusable element.
Do measure new screens against GitHub Desktop and Fork.
donts: Don't use dashboard cards, metric tiles or decorative illustration.
Don't use blue for anything but selection, focus, the primary action, tickets and hunk headers.
Don't show a state with colour alone, or an icon alone.
Don't add shadows to docked panes, rows or buttons.
Don't add uppercase tracked labels or kickers above headings; headings are sentence case at 12px/600 or larger.
Don't use typed glyphs or emoji as icons; icons are lucide SVGs.
